title: When train a small XGBoost model on DataBricks, it will crash and show memory issue. But similar table actually works well
question:
I meet a bug which blocks me a few days. I have a spark dataframe with 66 columns and 100K rows, I want to train a XGBoost model on DataBricks platform but will always crash. I generated a similar spark dataframe with 70 columns and 100K rows, in the same notebook it works great. I could not figure out why this happened. I already filled all the null values both in categorical or numeric columns from the table. My compute is 16.3 ML (includes Apache Spark 3.5.2, Scala 2.12) and 56GB memory and 16Core.

Below is the error I met, can anyone give me some help?

answer:
• check for hidden string columns: spark’s VectorAssembler needs all input columns to be numeric mismatched types often cause silent driver crashes or hangs. double-check your dataframe schema with .printSchema() and cast all features properly. see the official vector assembler docs for details.

  • control partition size: wide tables easily blow up executor memory if tasks are too big. coalesce or tune spark.sql.shuffle.partitions to balance parallelism and memory headroom monitor this in the spark ui. more tips in the spark tuning guide.

  • this subtle dtype + partition combo is the silent killer for spark xgboost jobs on medium-sized data.
